title: Screening for Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) in Adults
service: Screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection

criteria.text: Ordered by the beneficiary's primary care physician or practitioner within a primary care setting
criteria.span: when ordered by the beneficiary's primary care physician or practitioner within the context of a primary care setting

criteria.text: High risk: current or past illicit injection drug use, or blood transfusion before 1992
criteria.span: "High risk" is defined as persons with a current or past history of illicit injection drug use; and persons who have a history of receiving a blood transfusion prior to 1992.

criteria.text: Annual repeat screening only for continued illicit injection drug use since the prior negative test
criteria.span: Repeat screening for high risk persons is covered annually only for persons who have had continued illicit injection drug use since the prior negative screening test.

criteria.text: Not high risk: single screening test only if born 1945 through 1965
criteria.span: A single screening test is covered for adults who do not meet the high risk definition above, but who were born from 1945 through 1965.

criteria.text: Settings not considered primary care (ED, inpatient, ASC, IDTF, SNF, IRF, limited-focus clinics, hospice)
criteria.span: Emergency departments, inpatient hospital settings, ambulatory surgical centers, independent diagnostic testing facilities, skilled nursing facilities, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, clinics providing a limited focus of health care services, and hospice are examples of settings not considered primary care settings under this definition.

criteria.text: FDA-approved/cleared laboratory tests used per labeling and CLIA
criteria.span: CMS will cover screening for HCV with the appropriate U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved/cleared laboratory tests, used consistent with FDA-approved labeling and in compliance with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act regulations

notes: High risk is limited to current or past illicit injection drug use or a blood transfusion before 1992; other risk factors (tattoos, intranasal drug use, etc.) do not count under this NCD. Birth-cohort screening (born 1945 through 1965, inclusive) is a single lifetime test. 'Annually' for repeat screening is not defined in months, so repeat cases use intervals well over 12 months. Primary care physician/practitioner per §1833(u)(6) and §1833(x)(2)(A)(i).
